dna: Meditation music often follows natural breathing rhythms — slow volume swells and phrase lengths of 4–6 seconds guide the listener's inhale-exhale cycle.
Sudden changes break meditation. Music evolves glacially — introducing and removing elements over minutes rather than seconds, maintaining the trance state.
Singing bowls, crystal bowls, gongs, tanpura drones, and soft synth pads produce rich overtones that fill the mind without demanding analytical attention.
One or two sustained chords — often root and fifth — create a stable harmonic bed. Avoiding chord changes removes anticipation and allows the mind to rest.

Podcast music lives in precise time slots — 10–30 second intros, 3–5 second stings, and loopable beds. Precision matters more than complexity.

dna: The first 15–20 minutes are critical. Music begins warm and present, then slowly reduces in volume, brightness, and complexity to guide the brain into sleep stages.
Lower frequencies promote relaxation. Sleep music emphasizes sub-bass warmth and removes harsh high frequencies that trigger alertness.
No sudden changes in volume, timbre, or rhythm. Every transition is glacial — measured in minutes, not beats — to avoid waking the sleeping listener.
Sleep tracks run 30 minutes to 8 hours. A gradual fade-to-silence ensures the audio stops naturally without an abrupt ending that could wake the sleeper.
